missionsPage.title: Our Missions
missionsPage.scripture: And he said to them, "Go into all the world and proclaim the gospel to the whole creation. Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned. And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues; they will pick up serpents with their hands; and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not hurt them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will recover." So then the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God. And they went out and preached everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the message by accompanying signs.
missionsPage.intro:
The Righteous Vine Missions exists to carry the Gospel to the nations — reaching the unreached, strengthening the Church, and raising leaders who will disciple others long after we're gone. Since our founding in 2019, we've planted churches across Ghana, Kenya, and Liberia, and carried out mission work in Indonesia and Tanzania, building on years of field ministry that began in Monrovia in 2016.

Our work is guided by a simple conviction: every soul matters, and no distance — geographic or cultural — should stand between a person and the truth of Christ. From village outreaches in Alor and Sumba to church planting across West Africa, our missions combine evangelism, discipleship, and practical support — schools, clean water, medical outreach, and community development — so that the Gospel takes root not just in word, but in life.

We go where the need is greatest and the laborers are few, trusting that the same Vine that has sustained us will bear fruit in every place He sends us.

ghana.name: Ghana
ghana.title: Where It All Began
ghana.body:
It all began in Sweduru, a community in Ghana's Central Region, with a three-day outreach that would become the launchpad for our entire missions program. Partnering with Kings Life City Church, our team took to the streets — combining open-air crusade ministry, street evangelism, and radio preaching to reach the community with the Gospel.

God moved powerfully. The sick were healed, and those bound by mental illness were set free. By the end of the three days, over 100 souls had given their lives to Christ — each one handed over to Kings Life City Church for continued shepherding and discipleship. Sweduru wasn't just our first outreach; it was the proof of concept for everything TRVM has since become.

liberia.name: Liberia
liberia.title: A Church from an Abandoned Space
liberia.body:
In downtown Monrovia, inside an abandoned auditorium tucked within a charity school, a church was born — the Zoe Outreach Embassy. What started as a handful of people gathered together soon grew into a congregation of a hundred.

We went house to house, praying for the sick and setting the oppressed free. Soul winning wasn't an occasional effort here — it was daily, the very engine that kept the church moving forward. Youth, children, and the elderly all found their way in, and even those who hesitated to step through the door could still hear the Gospel carried through their windows. Out of an abandoned space, a beautiful church was born for the community.

indonesia.name: Indonesia
indonesia.title: Across the Islands
indonesia.body:
The call to Indonesia first came in 2017, but it would take five years before the Lord made a way. In 2022, NISOS Ministry in Michigan reached out after a passing mention in an earlier conversation — and this time, the timing was right. NISOS was ready to sponsor the mission, and the door finally opened.

That first trip was a one-month mission through North Sumatra, beginning in Kabanjahe and extending to towns and villages like Tarutung and Siborongborong, preaching in schools, churches, and communities along the way. Strangers became friends, and a bond was formed strong enough to carry the vision into 2023 — an extended mission that reached even further, into Sumba, Alor, Kupang, Bali, Sumatra, and Jakarta, marked by open-air crusades, home meetings, and church gatherings.

Hundreds of souls have come to Jesus across our Indonesia missions, with healings and miracles recorded at nearly every event, and the demon-possessed and oppressed set free. Among the most memorable moments was witnessing Hindu worshippers give their lives to Christ — both in Bali and in one of our meetings in Kabanjahe.

Since then, the Indonesia mission has grown into something lasting, with teams now forming across these islands for a continued, yearly mission presence. Indonesia's Muslim-majority context calls for a different kind of strategy — one centered on consistent discipleship and leadership training, built not just to win souls but to grow them, and to strengthen the Christian community for the long term.

kenya.name: Kenya
kenya.title: A Divine Connection
kenya.body:
In 2024, while praying over where to go next, a message arrived out of nowhere — Pastor Jerrison Machio Mapesa, reaching out on Facebook, ready to receive TRVM for missions in Kenya. It came at exactly the moment we needed direction, and we recognized it for what it was: a divine call. We answered it.

That first year in Kenya was a full month of ministry across villages, communities, and schools — reaching struggling churches in Malaha, Khaunga, Kakamega, and Shianda, and preaching in Eldoret and other cities. Every meeting brought tens of souls running to Jesus, alongside healing and miracles. In 2025, we extended the mission further, reaching even more areas for Christ, and made supporting smaller, struggling churches a core part of the work.

Out of that divine connection, a TRVM team in Kenya was born — led by Pastor Mapesa, a team of passionate soul winners and kingdom lovers now carrying the mission forward across East Africa.
